en.headline: Woman aged 66 loses HK$2.7 million in phone scam over alleged money laundering
en.dek: Police said the Ngau Tau Kok resident transferred the sum after a caller claimed her online insurance account was linked to money laundering.
body: Police received a report in the early hours of Saturday from a 66-year-old woman surnamed Chung living in On Kay Court in Ngau Tau Kok, who said she had lost HK$2.7 million in a telephone fraud.

According to police, the woman was contacted on Wednesday by a male caller who claimed she had previously purchased insurance online and alleged that her account was involved in money-laundering activities. He instructed her to transfer funds for investigative purposes.
She made two transfers, one of HK$2 million and one of HK$700,000, before later becoming suspicious and reporting the case. Police have classified the incident as fraud. No arrests have been made.
Officers reminded the public to remain alert to calls that impersonate insurance or banking staff and demand transfers under the pretext of investigations.

zh.headline: 牛頭角66歲婦遇電騙損失270萬元
zh.dek: 警方指事主接獲來電，聲稱其網上購買保險的戶口涉洗黑錢，遂按指示轉帳。
body: 警方今日凌晨接獲一名居於牛頭角安基苑、姓鍾的66歲婦人報案，指她遭電話騙案，損失270萬港元。
警方表示，事主於周三接獲一名男子來電，對方聲稱她曾在網上購買保險，並指其戶口涉嫌涉及洗黑錢活動，指示她轉帳以配合調查。
事主先後轉帳200萬元及70萬元後，始感可疑並報警。警方已將案件列作詐騙案處理，暫時未有人被捕。
警方提醒市民，遇到自稱保險或銀行職員並要求轉帳配合調查的來電，應提高警覺，切勿輕易轉帳。
